- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or after a sharp spike — model fails to correct downward quickly.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent highs; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for price peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, model often underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer for downward correction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day trends; use 10–15 day moving average as anchor for mid-term forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast volatility if sentiment is flat or declining — model tends to over-forecast volatility in low-sentiment periods.
